transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I just can't think clearly or make decisions the way I used to, and it's starting to affect my work and plans. It's gotten to the point where I'm having trouble just getting through my normal routines, so I figured I needed to get some help.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your thinking and daily routines, and have you had similar periods like this in the past?

This foggy, drained feeling has been my constant, everyday normal for about three years now, starting right after my work schedule shifted to irregular long-haul routes. I haven't had distinct periods like this in the past before that; it's just been one long, continuous stretch of feeling this way.

During these past three years, have you experienced any periods of a few weeks or more where your mood or energy felt significantly lower than your current baseline, or has it been a steady, consistent feeling throughout?

It has been a steady, consistent feeling the whole time rather than coming in waves. I honestly just came to accept this low, drained, and foggy state as my new normal, figuring it was just a consequence of getting older and working a demanding job. It never really lifted or changed; it's just been a constant weight.

Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition, such as a thyroid issue or sleep disorder, or have you noticed any other physical symptoms like changes in weight or body temperature during these past three years?

No, I've never been diagnosed with any medical conditions like thyroid issues. I also haven't noticed any physical changes like fluctuations in my weight or body temperature over these past three years.
Besides the fogginess and low energy, have you also experienced feelings of hopelessness, low self-esteem, or a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy over these past three years?

Yes, I definitely have. I constantly tell myself I'm just a washed-up truck driver who can't get ahead, and I've pretty much stopped showing up to softball and volunteering because I just don't have the interest anymore. It's left me feeling really empty, like I'm just going through the motions every day.

Have these feelings of hopelessness and loss of interest been so severe at any point that you felt unable to function at all, or have you consistently been able to maintain your basic daily responsibilities throughout these three years?

I haven’t completely shut down, but I’ve been barely scraping by. I've managed to keep working my driving routes, though I make more mistakes and feel totally drained, but I've lost the energy for anything else. My life has basically shrunk to just working and crashing on the couch, since I've dropped all my volunteering, softball, and career plans.

During these three years, have you ever experienced a period of two weeks or longer where your mood was so low or your interest in activities was so absent that it met the criteria for a major depressive episode, or has your mood remained consistently in this 'low' range without those deeper plunges?

It’s really been a steady, consistent low without any of those deeper plunges. It’s just been like a constant gray cloud sitting on me day in and day out since my work schedule changed three years ago. I haven't had times where it suddenly got much worse; it's just been this same flat, empty feeling the whole time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a chronic, persistent depressed mood lasting for three years, characterized by low energy, feelings of inadequacy, and loss of interest (anhedonia). Crucially, the patient denies any history of major depressive episodes (deeper plunges), and the state has been consistent and steady rather than episodic, which is the hallmark of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
